topics.title: Available AI Tools
topics.summary: ELM (Edinburgh access to Language Models) is the University of Edinburgh's AI innovation platform and a central gateway providing safer access to generative AI through large language models. The University of Edinburgh provides access to the Copilot chat service within Edge by signing in with University credentials, while full Microsoft 365 Copilot Office suite integration licenses are not currently provided. The University of Edinburgh encourages students to use ELM over external commercial AI platforms because its guidance states that data is not retained by third-party services to train models or for other purposes. March 2026 student guidance describes ELM as free to staff and students; another published entitlement page states discretionary School approval. Whether that approval condition still applies universally is not established by these sources. The full Microsoft 365 Copilot suite is not provided under the University's current institutional license agreement, and ISG currently has no plans to make the full Copilot for MS365 license available, though free Copilot chat within Edge is supported.

additionalTopics.title: Academic Integrity & Appeals
additionalTopics.summary: At the University of Edinburgh, presenting AI outputs as your own original work, machine-translating assessed work to English, submitting AI content without acknowledgment, and using AI agents within university learning platforms constitute academic misconduct. An appeal cannot be lodged until the Board of Examiners or decision-maker publishes its final decision in EUCLID Student View (as results on LEARN may not yet be ratified or moderated); appeals against academic decisions must be submitted promptly within 10 working days of the result being issued for undergraduate non-final years, and within 30 working days of the result being issued for undergraduate final year and all postgraduate taught and research students. Appeals against decisions of Student Discipline Officers or the Student Discipline Committee, and appeals against decisions of Fitness to Practise Panels, must be submitted within 10 working days of the receipt of the decision. Late appeals will only be considered in extraordinary circumstances explaining and evidencing why the deadline could not be met; appeals submitted over one year after the ratified or publication date of the original decision will not be considered under any circumstances.
additionalTopics.scope: Academic decisions by student category; Student Discipline and Fitness to Practise decisions have a different receipt trigger.
actions: Use the student-category deadline and the correct result-issued or decision-received trigger.
Check the source for late-appeal conditions and the one-year cutoff.

approved_tools.en: ELM (Edinburgh access to Language Models) is the University of Edinburgh's AI innovation platform and a central gateway providing safer access to generative AI through large language models. The University of Edinburgh provides access to the Copilot chat service within Edge by signing in with University credentials, while full Microsoft 365 Copilot Office suite integration licenses are not currently provided. The University of Edinburgh encourages students to use ELM over external commercial AI platforms because its guidance states that data is not retained by third-party services to train models or for other purposes. March 2026 student guidance describes ELM as free to staff and students; another published entitlement page states discretionary School approval. Whether that approval condition still applies universally is not established by these sources. The full Microsoft 365 Copilot suite is not provided under the University's current institutional license agreement, and ISG currently has no plans to make the full Copilot for MS365 license available, though free Copilot chat within Edge is supported.
approved_tools.zh: 大学提供 ELM 及使用大学账号登录的 Edge Copilot 聊天；当前机构许可不提供完整 Microsoft 365 Copilot 集成。2026年3月学生指引称 ELM 向师生免费，另一资格页面称须由学院酌情批准；该批准是否仍普遍适用尚未核实。工具访问不等于考核许可。

research_publication.en: Postgraduate research students who choose to use generative AI for aspects of assessed research (such as doctoral theses, MScR dissertations, or annual review submissions) should include a brief acknowledgment in the Declaration of Own Work at the start of the thesis or submission.

academic_integrity.en: At the University of Edinburgh, presenting AI outputs as your own original work, machine-translating assessed work to English, submitting AI content without acknowledgment, and using AI agents within university learning platforms constitute academic misconduct. An appeal cannot be lodged until the Board of Examiners or decision-maker publishes its final decision in EUCLID Student View (as results on LEARN may not yet be ratified or moderated); appeals against academic decisions must be submitted promptly within 10 working days of the result being issued for undergraduate non-final years, and within 30 working days of the result being issued for undergraduate final year and all postgraduate taught and research students. Appeals against decisions of Student Discipline Officers or the Student Discipline Committee, and appeals against decisions of Fitness to Practise Panels, must be submitted within 10 working days of the receipt of the decision. Late appeals will only be considered in extraordinary circumstances explaining and evidencing why the deadline could not be met; appeals submitted over one year after the ratified or publication date of the original decision will not be considered under any circumstances.
academic_integrity.zh: 将 AI 输出冒充原创构成学术不端。学术决定须待最终结果公布后申诉：本科非毕业年级为结果发布后10个工作日，本科毕业年级及全部授课型／研究型研究生为30个工作日。学生纪律及适任性决定的申诉为收到决定后10个工作日。逾期须有特别情形及证据；原决定核准或公布超过一年后不受理。

teaching_guidance.en: GenAI permissions at Edinburgh are set at assessment and course level; restrictions should be stated in the assessment task and students must consult their Course Organiser when unclear. The University of Edinburgh advises staff not to rely on AI detection tools to confirm authorship, as they misclassify human and AI content and there is no reliable automated provenance method.

security_procurement.en: For systematic or large-scale non-research adoption of AI or introduction of AI into existing platforms, staff must follow the approval process via the ISG Ethics Board, frame decisions using AI Impact Assessment guidance, and complete required impact assessments, including DPIA (Data Protection Impact Assessment) and EQIA (Equality Impact Assessment) where appropriate / as required (while research AI uses follow College Research Ethics Boards).

approved_tools.en: ELM (Edinburgh access to Language Models) is the University of Edinburgh's AI innovation platform and a central gateway providing safer access to generative AI through large language models. The University of Edinburgh provides access to the Copilot chat service within Edge by signing in with University credentials, while full Microsoft 365 Copilot Office suite integration licenses are not currently provided. The University of Edinburgh encourages students to use ELM over external commercial AI platforms because its guidance states that data is not retained by third-party services to train models or for other purposes. March 2026 student guidance describes ELM as free to staff and students; another published entitlement page states discretionary School approval. Whether that approval condition still applies universally is not established by these sources. The full Microsoft 365 Copilot suite is not provided under the University's current institutional license agreement, and ISG currently has no plans to make the full Copilot for MS365 license available, though free Copilot chat within Edge is supported.

academic_integrity.en: At the University of Edinburgh, presenting AI outputs as your own original work, machine-translating assessed work to English, submitting AI content without acknowledgment, and using AI agents within university learning platforms constitute academic misconduct. An appeal cannot be lodged until the Board of Examiners or decision-maker publishes its final decision in EUCLID Student View (as results on LEARN may not yet be ratified or moderated); appeals against academic decisions must be submitted promptly within 10 working days of the result being issued for undergraduate non-final years, and within 30 working days of the result being issued for undergraduate final year and all postgraduate taught and research students. Appeals against decisions of Student Discipline Officers or the Student Discipline Committee, and appeals against decisions of Fitness to Practise Panels, must be submitted within 10 working days of the receipt of the decision. Late appeals will only be considered in extraordinary circumstances explaining and evidencing why the deadline could not be met; appeals submitted over one year after the ratified or publication date of the original decision will not be considered under any circumstances.

academic_integrity.meaningEn: Academic decisions by student category; Student Discipline and Fitness to Practise decisions have a different receipt trigger.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 学术决定按学生类别区分；学生纪律及适任性决定从收到决定起算。
